title: FICO v2: what the pilot showed

cues: press 1: under the strip of 20 squares ("5 October", "24 October", "Each square is one day."), the answer: "Scores now come from what the coach saw; it is not finished, and we give it to more coaches in steps."
press 2: moves to p02
note.body:
**Coaches have scored lessons a new way for three weeks; here is what happened.**
Three weeks ago coaches stopped checking a form Rumi filled in, and started writing what they saw. So, did it work, and what do we do now?
(press)
The short answer: scores now come from what the coach saw; it is not finished, and we give it to more coaches in steps. The next nine screens show why, one answer each. Every number behind them is in the appendix.
[Presenter, in your own words: why a fair score matters to the teacher who is observed next week.]
(press)
note.first_line: **Coaches have scored lessons a new way for three weeks; here is what happened.** Three weeks ago coaches stopped checking a form Rumi filled in, and started writing what they saw.

cues: press 1: the old-form still, "The old form: 37 scores, every one already filled in"
press 2: the grid of 100 dots, "left as Rumi set it" and "changed by the coach", with "86 of every 100 scores Rumi filled in were left as they were"
press 3: "Leaders believed coaches disagreed with each other more than with Rumi; nobody had measured it."
press 4: moves to p03
note.body:
**The old form came already filled in by Rumi; coaches left most scores unchanged.**
(press)
This is the old form. Rumi listened to the recording and filled in all 37 scores before the coach had said a word.
(press)
Across all coaches on the old form, out of every 100 scores Rumi filled in, 86 were left exactly as they were. And 41 forms in 100 went back inside five minutes. So a score often told the teacher what Rumi guessed, not what the coach saw.
(press)
We also believed coaches disagreed with each other more than with Rumi. Nobody had ever measured that. The new form lets us.
(press)
note.first_line: **The old form came already filled in by Rumi; coaches left most scores unchanged.** This is the old form.

cues: press 1: phone screen 2, "After the lesson": "A checklist of 17 things the teacher does, down from 37, such as who gets to answer."
press 2: phone screen 3, "Then the coach sends the form": "They pick the one thing the teacher should improve next and send the form, so Rumi's quotes cannot change their scores."
press 3: phone screen 4, "Only then, Rumi": "Rumi then shows short quotes from the recording, each for the coach to agree or disagree with."
press 4: moves to p04
note.body:
**The coach now writes what they see first; then Rumi shows quotes to check.**
[Say: these phone screens are mock-ups; no real teacher, child or school is on them.]
The form starts blank. During the lesson the coach types simple counts as they watch.
(press)
After the lesson comes a checklist of 17 things the teacher does, down from 37, such as who gets to answer, each in plain words.
(press)
Then the coach picks the one thing the teacher should improve next, and sends the form, so Rumi's quotes cannot change their scores.
(press)
Only then does Rumi show short quotes from the recording, each for the coach to agree or disagree with. The recording comes afterwards, and only as a check. Rumi can no longer put words in the coach's mouth.
(press)
note.first_line: **The coach now writes what they see first; then Rumi shows quotes to check.** The form starts blank.

cues: press 1: 12 coach marks and 223 visit dots, "12 coaches, 223 visits in three weeks"
press 2: three reader marks beside one recording, "It scored each recording without seeing the coach's scores, so we could compare the two."
press 3: pairs of coach marks over one classroom, "On 13 lessons two coaches scored the same class separately"
press 4: moves to p05
note.body:
**Twelve coaches used the new form; a second AI, not Rumi, scored the recordings.**
(press)
Twelve coaches used the new form most, and between them made 223 visits in three weeks.
(press)
A second AI, not Rumi, also scored the recorded lessons. It scored each recording without seeing the coach's scores, so we could compare the two.
(press)
And 13 times, two coaches scored the same lesson separately, so we can see whether they agree. Because that is AI too, a person checks it next; that is the last scene.
(press)
note.first_line: **Twelve coaches used the new form; a second AI, not Rumi, scored the recordings.** Twelve coaches used the new form most, and between them made 223 visits in three weeks.

cues: press 1: two bars, "Same lesson: about 6 in 10 scores match." and "Different lessons: about 5 in 10. This is what guessing gives."
press 2: the 13 pairs of shapes, 6 filled under "same", 7 plain under "different", "Not yet well enough: on the one thing the teacher should improve next, pairs agreed only about half the time."
press 3: "We cannot compare with the old form: Rumi filled it in first, so coaches never scored it alone."
press 4: "If coaches keep pairing up as they do now, we will know more by about 6 November."
press 5: moves to p06
note.body:
**Two coaches now agree better than guessing, but not yet well enough.**
[Say: two coaches, one lesson; no teacher, coach or school is named.]
First, the better than guessing.
(press)
When two coaches score the same lesson, about 6 in 10 of their scores match. For two different lessons it is about 5 in 10, and that is what guessing gives. The gap is small, but it is clearly there.
(press)
Now the not well enough. This is a different question: each coach picks the one thing the teacher should improve next. On that, pairs agreed only about half the time; the filled pairs are the ones that matched. Our plan asked for 7 in 10.
(press)
We cannot compare with the old form, because Rumi filled it in first, so two coaches never scored a lesson on their own.
(press)
If coaches keep pairing up as they do now, we will know more by about 6 November. The full figures are on appendix page 10.
(press)
note.first_line: **Two coaches now agree better than guessing, but not yet well enough.** First, the better than guessing.

scenes.title: What can a recording alone judge?

cues: press 1: 17 boxes, 12 discs "coach in the room" and 5 triangles "nobody can judge these well until the form changes", with "Each box is one of the 17 things."
press 2: "The second AI was not good enough on any. Twelve need a coach in the room; five need the form fixed first."
press 3: a drawn camera, "Photos as coaches took them made no clear difference." and "Asking coaches for particular photos has not been tried yet."
press 4: moves to p07
note.body:
**Nothing on the form can yet be judged from the recording alone.**
For each of the 17 things, we asked: does the AI, working from the recording alone, agree with the coach well beyond guessing?
(press)
Each box is one of the 17 things coaches look for. None of them can be judged from a recording alone yet.
(press)
The second AI was not good enough on any of them. Twelve need a coach in the room, such as who gets to answer. The other five need the form fixed first: as it stands, not even two coaches in the room can judge them well. The closest is group work, and even there the AI falls just short. And no person has checked the AI yet.
(press)
Photos, as coaches took them, made no clear difference. Asking coaches for particular photos has not been tried yet. All 17 are listed on appendix page 5.
(press)
note.first_line: **Nothing on the form can yet be judged from the recording alone.** For each of the 17 things, we asked: does the AI, working from the recording alone, agree with the coach well beyond guessing?

cues: press 1: standing caption "the 12 coaches who used the new form most"; the time picture (drawn, no caption): during the lesson nothing before and about 7 minutes now; after the lesson about 7 minutes before and about 3 now
press 2: two bars, "about 7 minutes" before and "about 11 minutes" now, "A visit now takes a few minutes longer."
press 3: a third bar, "later visits", "about 8 minutes" ("now" fades and loses its label), "Later visits: still longer than before."
press 4: moves to p08
note.body:
**Coaches spend about 7 minutes more during the lesson, about 4 fewer after.**
These are the 12 coaches who used the new form most.
(press)
During the lesson the old form asked nothing; the new one takes about 7 minutes of phone work. After the lesson, the work fell from about 7 minutes to about 3.
(press)
So in all, a whole visit went from about 7 minutes to about 11, a few minutes longer. These are typical times, so the parts do not add up exactly.
(press)
And coaches get faster. In later visits, from a coach's sixteenth form on, a whole visit takes about 8 minutes, still longer than before. We cannot see a fall in visits a week, though three weeks is too short to rule one out. Appendix page 14 has it all.
(press)
note.first_line: **Coaches spend about 7 minutes more during the lesson, about 4 fewer after.** These are the 12 coaches who used the new form most.

note.body:
**The quotes Rumi picks from lessons are now right about 9 times in 10.**
[Say: one lesson's quote at most; no teacher, child or school is named.]
These are the short quotes Rumi picks out of a recording, such as a child explaining why.
(press)
Before Rumi was fixed on 16 October, about 4 in 10 of those quotes were what Rumi said they were.
(press)
Since the fix, about 9 in 10 are, as judged by the AI. A person checks that this week.
(press)
Right, but ask Rumi twice about one lesson and at least half its quotes differ. Each quote it picks is usually right; it just picks different ones each time. So scores should come from the whole lesson, not single quotes.
(press)
note.first_line: **The quotes Rumi picks from lessons are now right about 9 times in 10.** These are the short quotes Rumi picks out of a recording, such as a child explaining why.

cues: press 1: the three coach stones, "Known fixes include recordings that get lost."
press 2: the stone "new wording", "New wording for all 17 things is drafted. Teachers see no new scores until it is checked."
press 3: the stone "coaching for teachers", "Rumi also coaches teachers on their own recordings. That coaching will use the new form, hidden from teachers until checked."
press 4: moves to p10
note.body:
**Fix the form, test it with 12 more coaches, then give it to everyone.**
Every answer today comes with a condition, so the plan is in steps.
(press)
First we fix what we know is broken: recordings that get lost, visits linked to the wrong lesson plan, and a few more on appendix page 12. Then two weeks with 12 more coaches. Then every coach.
(press)
New wording for all 17 things is drafted, and none is dropped. Teachers see no new scores until it is checked. First we score the 166 visits coaches already checked again, and show teachers old and new side by side.
(press)
Rumi also coaches teachers on their own recordings. That coaching will use the new form, hidden from teachers until a person has checked it.
[Presenter, in your own words: what you ask of coaches over the next two weeks.]
(press)
note.first_line: **Fix the form, test it with 12 more coaches, then give it to everyone.** Every answer today comes with a condition, so the plan is in steps.

cues: press 1: the 74 cards and "This person trains coaches, did not use the new form, and will not see the coaches' scores"

note.body:
**This week one person spends an hour checking 74 quotes Rumi picked from lessons.**
(press)
[Say: one quote, one lesson; no teacher, child or school is named.]
This person trains coaches, did not use the new form, and will not see the coaches' scores.
(press)
It checks quotes coaches agreed with. If 5 or more in 100 are wrong, the next 12 coaches wait until Rumi's quotes are fixed. 9 in 10 right sounds like 1 in 10 wrong, but that is one AI reader's view; the person's check decides.
(press)
Afterwards the same person reads six whole lessons, a second check on what we found. It could change our answers on how many children spoke, getting the facts right and the teacher's questions.
(press)
note.first_line: **This week one person spends an hour checking 74 quotes Rumi picked from lessons.** This person trains coaches, did not use the new form, and will not see the coaches' scores.
